text:
Jordan_C: Hey team, hitting an odd OAuth failure for a customer. After GitHub/Google auth we get a 404 on our callback and the app logs show no state cookie. Example redirect we received from the provider: 
https://app.example.com/auth/callback%2Fprofile?code=ABCD&state=xyz123

Iana (support): Thanks — can you paste the full redirect URL and any server logs? Is this only GitHub or Google too? :thinking:

Jordan_C: Both. Repro steps: 1) User clicks login from /profile 2) We set a session cookie at path `/auth` and build redirect URI like: `BASE/auth/callback/${encodeURIComponent(returnPath)}` 3) Provider redirects to `.../auth/callback%2Fprofile?code=...&state=...` 4) Our app returns 404 and state cookie missing in logs.

Jordan_C: Quick curl of the incoming request we captured:
```\nGET /auth/callback%2Fprofile?code=ABCD&state=xyz123 HTTP/1.1
Host: app.example.com
Cookie: session=eyJ...; other=val
```

Olga (eng): Hmm — looks like the provider is sending the encoded slash in the path. Many reverse proxies or routers will decode `%2F` to `/` before routing which can change the perceived path segment. If the decoded path becomes `/auth/callback/profile` our route for `/auth/callback` won't match and the request can be handled by a different vhost or return 404. Also important: cookies are scoped by path — if we set cookie Path=/auth then `/auth/callback/profile` still matches, but if the proxy rewrites or forwards to a different backend it might strip or change cookies.

Maya (sre): Confirming: Edge/ALB/Cloudflare often normalize paths. We see this with Cloudflare Workers where default behavior can normalize percent-encoded slashes. ALB/Nginx may also unescape paths depending on config. Two likely failure modes here: 1) path decoding causes route mismatch -> 404, 2) request gets routed to another backend that doesn't have the session cookie (so state missing), leading to PKCE/state mismatch.

Iana (support): Customer says the OAuth app redirect URI they registered is `https://app.example.com/auth/callback/%2Fprofile` (they followed our old pattern). Can they change it? Quick workaround to recommend?

Olga (eng): Best immediate fix: don't embed return paths in the path portion. Use a query param. Example: set redirect URI to `https://app.example.com/auth/callback?next=%2Fprofile` and build redirect with `?next=${encodeURIComponent(returnPath)}`. That avoids relying on encoded slashes in the path and is robust across proxies.

Maya (sre): For long-term, SRE can check edge config: ensure the LB/proxy preserves encoded slashes (e.g., disable automatic unescape/normalization) and make sure cookie forwarding is consistent. On Nginx look for path normalization rewrites; on Cloudflare check Workers/router settings. Also check if any CDN rule strips query parameters when path contains encoded chars.

Jordan_C: Logs from our app when the 404 occurs: `router: no route for /auth/callback/profile` and our error shows `state cookie not found` in the PKCE handler. So it definitely decoded to `/auth/callback/profile` somewhere upstream.

Olga (eng): Quick patch suggestion for our code base: change redirect builder from:
```\nconst redirect = `${BASE_URL}/auth/callback/${encodeURIComponent(returnPath)}`
```
to:
```\nconst redirect = `${BASE_URL}/auth/callback?next=${encodeURIComponent(returnPath)}`
```
Also make sure we validate `next` on callback to prevent open redirect abuses.

Maya (sre): Action items: 1) I'll inspect edge/ALB logs for requests around `3632105555` and confirm whether path was decoded before hitting backend. 2) If edge is normalizing we can add a passthrough rule or adjust router.

Iana (support): I'll tell the customer the workaround: update their registered redirect URI to `https://app.example.com/auth/callback` and then have the app send `?next=%2Fprofile` on initial auth start. Also ask them to clear any intermediate proxies/caches and retry.

Jordan_C: Confirmed: after switching to query param flow locally the OAuth roundtrip works and state is preserved. Thanks everyone. :tada:

Olga (eng): We'll still follow up to make the code change in master and include a note in troubleshooting docs about encoded slashes + OAuth state.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch `fix/oauth-next-param` — will run canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC. :rocket:

Maya (sre): Leaving a note here for infra: check if any customers could be affected by redirect URIs that use percent-encoded slashes (search logs for `%2Fprofile` or `%2Fdashboard`). If we find more, reach out with the recommended `next` migration.

Iana (support): Filed support ticket update to customer and added reproduction steps + recommended workaround. Ticket #SUP-9281.
